label: The Cartan-Hadamard Theorem
notes: This chapter, printed pages 193 through 204, lifts an upper curvature bound from the local scale to the global one. We open with the headline: a complete, simply connected, locally CAT(zero) length space is globally CAT(zero), and we preview the universal cover as the device that makes this possible for the merely local case.

label: Local vs Global CAT(k)
notes: Here we separate two notions students often conflate. Local CAT(k) means every point owns a small ball satisfying the comparison inequality, while global CAT(k) demands the inequality everywhere on geodesics joining arbitrary points. The chapter is exactly the bridge between these two scales when curvature is non-positive.

label: The Theorem Statement
notes: We state the metric Cartan-Hadamard theorem precisely. For k at most zero, a complete, simply connected, locally CAT(k) space is globally CAT(k). I stress each hypothesis aloud: completeness, simple connectivity, the local bound, and the sign restriction on k, since dropping any one of them breaks the conclusion.

label: Why Simple Connectivity
notes: This slide motivates the topological hypothesis with the flat torus. The torus is locally CAT(zero) yet has many geodesics between points and is not globally CAT(zero). Its universal cover, the Euclidean plane, repairs everything. Simple connectivity is precisely what rules out the homotopically distinct competing geodesics that monodromy would create.

label: The Universal Cover Unwraps
notes: We picture the covering projection from the plane onto the torus. Loops downstairs unroll to non-closed paths upstairs, so a single pair of points upstairs is joined by exactly one local geodesic. I connect this picture to the lab artifact, the patchwork lift, where lifted triangles show monodromy disappearing once the base is simply connected.

label: Local Geodesics and Development
notes: We define local geodesics and the developing idea. A locally geodesic path is straightened patch by patch against the model space. The Cartan-Hadamard construction develops these local geodesics into honest geodesics in the cover, building the global comparison out of overlapping local comparisons glued along the path.

label: The Local-to-Global Principle
notes: This is the engine of the proof. The local-to-global principle says that in a complete simply connected space where the comparison holds locally and small loops contract, local geodesics are globally unique and the CAT(k) inequality propagates. I describe how convexity of the local metric chains along a path to a global convexity statement.

label: Uniqueness of Geodesics
notes: Here we record the central output: in the universal cover any two points are joined by a unique geodesic, varying continuously with its endpoints. I explain that uniqueness follows from convexity of the distance function, which forbids two distinct geodesics with the same endpoints, and underwrites the contraction we build next.

label: Convexity of the Metric
notes: We make convexity quantitative. Along two geodesics issuing from a common point the distance grows convexly, captured by the CAT(zero) inequality on the comparison triangle. This convex behaviour of the metric is both the certificate of the upper bound and the tool that produces unique geodesics and the geodesic contraction.

label: Contractibility and Asphericity
notes: We harvest the topological consequences. Because geodesics to a basepoint are unique and depend continuously on the endpoint, sliding along them gives a deformation retraction, so the cover is contractible. Hence the original space is aspherical: all higher homotopy groups vanish and it is a classifying space for its fundamental group.

label: Generalisation and Scope
notes: We state the general form. The universal cover of any complete, connected, locally CAT(k) space with k at most zero is globally CAT(k). I note where the sign matters: positive k forces a diameter bound from the model sphere, so the unrestricted lifting argument is special to non-positive curvature.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We consolidate the logical chain: local bound plus completeness plus simple connectivity yields global CAT(k), unique geodesics, convex metric, and contractibility. I preview how this theorem feeds the study of fundamental groups acting on CAT(zero) spaces and the rigidity results that occupy the remainder of Part II.
